findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `_finish_bootstrap` applies to the attach arm, either by recording the arm in the pending file or by confirming every step matches today's attach behaviour, and add a test for the attach-arm resume.
evidence: "The orphan arm's tail (user config, `commit.gpgsign`/`tag.gpgsign` false, the initial empty commit) moves into a `_finish_bootstrap(repo, tracker)` helper"

findings.finding: The plan does not say whether `_finish_bootstrap` runs when the pending file was left by the attach-to-existing-branch arm. On the mounted path it would then set `commit.gpgsign`/`tag.gpgsign` to false and commit `.pre-commit-config.yaml` on an existing shared ticket branch. Today those steps belong to the orphan arm's tail, so the plan does not establish that the attach flow already does this.
scenarios: Init times out after attaching to an existing remote ticket branch. The next init applies orphan-only config and commits to the shared branch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which branch paths call `_finish_bootstrap`, and keep the orphan-only steps (gpgsign writes, root commit) on orphan creation: record the path in the pending file, or have a resume run them only when the tracker's HEAD is unborn.
evidence: Plan: "The orphan arm's tail (user config, `commit.gpgsign`/`tag.gpgsign` false, the initial empty commit) moves into a `_finish_bootstrap(repo, tracker)` helper that also runs ..."
init.py:384-385: gpgsign writes run only after the orphan `worktree add`; the local, remote and advertised paths return 0 at 319/338/358 without them
search for `worktreeConfig` in src/rebar: no matches, so tracker `git config` writes land in the common config
The plan does not say what the pending file contains, so a resume cannot tell a stopped attach from a stopped create
findings.finding: The pending file is written before `_mount_or_create_branch` for every branch path (local, remote-tracking, advertised, orphan), but it does not record which path ran. `_finish_bootstrap` bundles steps that today run only when creating an orphan branch (`commit.gpgsign`/`tag.gpgsign` false, the root commit) with the steps every mount runs. The plan does not say whether a fresh attach calls `_finish_bootstrap`, or whether a resume after an attach-path stop applies the orphan-only gpgsign writes. Those writes also reach beyond the tracker. Nothing enables `extensions.worktreeConfig` (no match in src/rebar), so `git -C tracker config commit.gpgsign false` writes the shared `.git/config` and turns off signing for the host repo too. Extending it to attach mounts is an unstated widening of what the change touches.
findings.location: Approach step 6 (`_finish_bootstrap` contents and when it is called) / src/rebar/_commands/init.py:373-395
scenarios: A user attaches to an existing remote `tickets` branch; the attach stalls after `worktree add`, and the next init resumes. `_finish_bootstrap` sets `commit.gpgsign=false` in the host repo's shared config, which an attach never did before.
If the fresh-path code calls `_finish_bootstrap` after every successful mount, every attach now disables host-repo signing.
findings.suggested_fix: Split `_finish_bootstrap` into steps shared by every mount (user config, scratch exclude, precommit, local files) and orphan-only steps (gpgsign false plus the root commit). Run the orphan-only steps only when the tracker's HEAD is unborn, which identifies a create that has not finished, and say explicitly that attach paths never write gpgsign.

findings.finding: Commands other than `rebar init` do not consult the pending file. A store left with the pending file is still a mounted tracker, so `rebar create` and similar commands run against it. That can make the first commit before the next `rebar init`. Then `_finish_bootstrap` skips the initial commit because HEAD is no longer unborn, and the 'root commit is `chore: initialize ticket tracker`' guarantee fails.
scenarios: Init times out after `worktree add --orphan`. The user ignores the message and runs `rebar create`. A later `rebar init` finds HEAD born and never makes the init commit. `commit.gpgsign` may also be unset for the intervening commit.
findings.suggested_fix: In the common store-open path, if `ticket-init.pending` exists, exit with 'Error: rebar init did not finish; re-run rebar init' before any write.

findings.finding: Step 6 assumes it is safe to resume on the already-mounted path ('All steps are already idempotent or guarded'). But that path runs before the init lock is taken. A second `rebar init`, possibly from a linked worktree whose tracker symlinks to the same store, can see the pending file while the first init is still bootstrapping under the lock, and run `_finish_bootstrap` at the same time. Both may find HEAD unborn and both make the initial commit, or race on `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. The idempotence guards are check-then-act and are not safe under concurrency without the lock.
scenarios: Main-worktree init is between `worktree add --orphan` and the initial commit. A concurrent `rebar init` in the main or a linked worktree sees the tracker mounted and the pending file present, runs _finish_bootstrap, and both processes commit 'chore: initialize ticket tracker'.
The concurrent run removes the pending file while the first init is still bootstrapping, then the first init fails, so nothing is left to trigger the next resume.
findings.suggested_fix: On the already-mounted path, when the pending file exists, acquire the init lock, re-test the pending file, run _finish_bootstrap, remove the file, and release the lock in a finally before the ensure sweep.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 2, state that ensure-sweep timeouts are absorbed by run_ensures (ensures.py:153), and decide whether init_core should turn a sweep outcome stopped by GitTimedOut into rc 1 with the re-run message or keep rc 0 with a WARNING.
evidence: ensures.py:153-158: `except GitTimedOut as exc: ... outcomes.append(EnsureOutcome(uid, "failed", detail)); break`
init.py:98-105: _run_ensures_logged only emits a WARNING for failed outcomes
Plan step 2: "init_core catches `GitTimedOut` once, at the top ... The first timeout therefore ends init"
findings.finding: Step 2 says init_core's top-level catch means 'The first timeout therefore ends init'. But init_core's ensure sweep goes through run_ensures, which catches GitTimedOut itself (ensures.py:153), records the unit as 'failed', and stops. The timeout never reaches the new catch, so init still prints 'Ticket system initialized.' or 'already initialized' with rc 0. The plan does not mention this or say whether it is intended.
scenarios: A stall starts after bootstrap: the sweep's first config call times out, a WARNING is printed, and init reports success with rc 0.
Mounted re-init on a stall that begins after the first rev-parse: rc 0 'already initialized' rather than the plan's 'Re-run rebar init' error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Testing, name the exact seams the stall stub must patch (`rebar._commands.init.run_git_write` and `rebar._commands._init_ensures.run_git_write`, plus `run_git` if any probe still uses it) and count calls across both.
evidence: init.py:40 `from rebar._store.gitutil import run_git, run_git_write` gives init its own binding
test_ensure_git_timeout.py patches only `_init_ensures.run_git_write`
Plan: "Unit tests stub `run_git_write` to return the watchdog's own result (code 124), as tests/unit/test_ensure_git_timeout.py does"
findings.finding: The testing approach says to 'stub `run_git_write`' as test_ensure_git_timeout.py does, but init has two separate bindings. init.py imports its own `run_git_write` (line 40), while the pin runs through `_init_ensures.run_git_write`, the binding that test file patches. On a fresh init the first git call is the pin's `config --get` through `_init_ensures`. 'Exactly 1 git call' and 'no tracker directory exists' only hold if both module bindings, plus `run_git` for the fetch and probe seams, are stubbed.
scenarios: A test patches only init.run_git_write: the pin's config calls run for real, and the counted 'first call' is a different operation than the plan states.
A test patches only _init_ensures.run_git_write: the 'already-initialized rev-parse stalled' case never stalls.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a shared fixture that monkeypatches both `init.run_git_write` and `_init_ensures.run_git_write` with one stall stub that appends to a single call list.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resume `_finish_bootstrap` only while holding the init lock, and re-check that the pending file exists after taking the lock, so a resume never runs at the same time as a live bootstrap.
evidence: Plan: "On the already-mounted path, when the pending file exists, init runs `_finish_bootstrap`, removes the file, then runs the ensure sweep as today."
Plan: "it makes the initial commit only while the tracker's HEAD is unborn" — a check-then-act guard
init.py:154-182: the mounted/idempotency branch returns before `_acquire_init_lock` (init.py:200-201)
Plan step 6 writes the pending file before `_mount_or_create_branch`, so it exists for the whole of a live, healthy bootstrap, not only after a crash
findings.finding: The resume path in step 6 runs `_finish_bootstrap` (config writes plus the 'initial commit only while HEAD is unborn' check) on the already-mounted path. In init_core that path returns before the init lock is taken (init.py:154-182; lock at 200-204). An init that is still running also holds the pending file. So a second `rebar init` started during another process's bootstrap sees a mounted tracker and the pending file, and runs `_finish_bootstrap` at the same time. The unborn-HEAD guard is a check-then-act race (TOCTOU): both processes can see an unborn HEAD and both try the root commit and the precommit commit. The second process can also remove the pending file while the first is still mid-bootstrap.
findings.location: Approach step 6 (resume on the already-mounted path) / src/rebar/_commands/init.py:154-204
scenarios: Two terminals (or a script and a user) run `rebar init` at about the same time on a fresh repo. B sees A's tracker after A's `worktree add --orphan` and before A's root commit. Both commit, or one fails on the ref lock, and B removes the pending file under A.
A's bootstrap times out later; B has already removed the marker, so the next init will not resume.
findings.suggested_fix: On the already-mounted path, when the pending file exists, acquire `_init_lock_dir(repo)` with `_acquire_init_lock`, re-check that the pending file still exists, then run `_finish_bootstrap`, remove the file, and release the lock in a `finally`. If the lock cannot be acquired, report it and return 1 rather than resuming without the lock.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In `_finish_bootstrap`, check the return codes of the root commit and the precommit add/commit; on failure report it, return 1, and keep the pending file so the next init resumes.
evidence: Plan: "removes it only after the bootstrap completes" — completion is not defined in terms of the commits succeeding
Context: "the `commit.gpgsign`/`tag.gpgsign` writes in `_mount_or_create_branch` discard their results"
init.py:386-394 and 467-475: `_git(...)` results are discarded
findings.finding: Step 1 covers only timeouts. `_finish_bootstrap` still ignores the result of the root `commit --allow-empty` and the `_commit_precommit` add/commit, as today (init.py:386-394, 467-475). If one fails for a reason other than a timeout (rc != 0 but not 124, e.g. a ref-lock or permission or disk error), the plan still counts the bootstrap as 'completed' and removes the pending file. The tracker is then left with no init commit and an untracked `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and the next init will not resume. That is the same permanent half-initialized state the plan is meant to fix, reached through a different failure.
findings.location: Approach step 6 ("removes it only after the bootstrap completes") / src/rebar/_commands/init.py:386-394, 463-475
scenarios: The root commit fails with a non-timeout error; init prints 'initialized', removes the marker, and later commits become the branch root, as in the reproduction's third case.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `_finish_bootstrap` return an rc: if the root commit, the precommit `add`/`commit` or the gpgsign writes return non-zero, write the stderr and return 1 without removing the pending file. `init_core` removes the file only when `_finish_bootstrap` returns 0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that init checks for an existing pending file before writing a new one, and writes it only on the create/attach path, so a healthy re-init never runs `_finish_bootstrap`.
evidence: "init writes a `ticket-init.pending` file ... before `_mount_or_create_branch`"
"On the already-mounted path, when the pending file exists, init runs `_finish_bootstrap`"
"Without the file, re-init behaves as today."
The mounted check (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, init.py:186-188) appears to sit inside `_mount_or_create_branch`, after the write point.
findings.finding: The plan does not say how the pending-file write is ordered relative to the already-mounted check. The file is written 'before `_mount_or_create_branch`', but the already-mounted branch only runs `_finish_bootstrap` 'when the pending file exists'. If the write happens unconditionally before `_mount_or_create_branch`, the file always exists on re-init, so `_finish_bootstrap` runs on every re-init. That contradicts 'Without the file, re-init behaves as today'.
scenarios: Healthy re-init of a fully bootstrapped store writes the pending file, sees it, and re-runs user config, gpgsign, the precommit commit and local-file generation every time.
findings.suggested_fix: Read `pending_existed = pending_path.exists()` at lock acquisition. Write the file only when the tracker is not yet mounted (the create/attach arm). On the mounted path, run `_finish_bootstrap` only if `pending_existed`. Add a test: a healthy re-init with no pending file makes zero `_finish_bootstrap` git calls.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a timed-out network probe is handled: either it ends init like `GitTimedOut`, or AC2 is reworded to 'at most one local git bound plus the remote probe bound'. Add a test with a remote configured.
evidence: "The network probe (`probe_remote_branch`, `run_bounded_git`) keeps its own `REMOTE_PROBE_TIMEOUT`."
"A stalled filesystem costs `rebar init` at most one git bound before it reports the failure."
findings.finding: AC2 ('at most one git bound') conflicts with step 4, which keeps `probe_remote_branch`/`run_bounded_git` on its own `REMOTE_PROBE_TIMEOUT`. The plan does not say whether a timed-out network probe raises `GitTimedOut` or is read as 'unreachable' and init continues. If init continues, a stall can cost the probe timeout plus one write bound.
findings.location: Approach step 4 vs Acceptance Criteria line 2
scenarios: A repo with an origin remote on a stalled filesystem: `ls-remote`/the probe stalls until `REMOTE_PROBE_TIMEOUT`, init treats the remote as unreachable, then the next local write stalls for 120 s.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either confirm in the plan that both probe functions already accept `run_git_fn`, or add `src/rebar/_commands/_init_probe.py` (adding the injectable parameter, defaulting to `run_git`) to Scope.
evidence: "init passes a `run_git_fn` adapter over `_git` to `_init_probe.remote_exists` and `require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote`"
"src/rebar/_commands/_init_probe.py:77-99" run through `run_git`
Scope: "src/rebar/_commands/init.py — steps 1-4 and 6."

The plan cites these functions as calling `run_git` directly (`_init_probe.py:77-99`). If they do not already accept a `run_git_fn` parameter, `src/rebar/_commands/_init_probe.py` must change, and it is not in Scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what the next `rebar init` does with an in-progress rebase left by a timed-out `rebase --continue`, and add a second-init test asserting it recovers (rc 0, no rebase in progress).
evidence: "a timed-out `rebase --continue` is not followed by `rebase --abort`"
The test only asserts "returns 1 with no `rebase --abort` call".
findings.finding: Re-raising `GitTimedOut` from rebase recovery deliberately leaves the tracker mid-rebase. The plan does not say what the next `rebar init` does with that state, and no test covers it. The user is told to 're-run rebar init', but the plan gives no evidence that re-init resumes or aborts a dangling rebase safely.
scenarios: After a filesystem stall the tracker has `.git/rebase-merge` present; the next init's ensure sweep or commits fail or behave unexpectedly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for `<op>`, for example the git subcommand plus first argument taken from `GitTimedOut`'s argv field, and assert that exact string in the test.
evidence: "Error: git <op> timed out during rebar init; nothing after it ran."
findings.finding: The error message template uses `<op>` without saying where it comes from (for example a field on `GitTimedOut`, or the git argv subcommand). The test asserts that stderr 'names the operation', so the executor has to choose the format.
scenarios: The executor prints the full argv in one place and a subcommand elsewhere; the test asserts a different string.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition per altered arm: init_core catch, _create_tracker exit, and the best-effort auto-init path. Say whether a timeout is transient/retryable, which exit code signals it, and what the best-effort path surfaces.
evidence: "writes `Error: git <op> timed out during rebar init; nothing after it ran. Re-run 'rebar init' to finish.` and returns 1"
"`_create_tracker` catches it, reports it, and exits 1"
"The best-effort path at _cli/_init.py:176-180 already catches `Exception`."
findings.finding: The plan alters several failure arms but does not label any of them with an explicit disposition (transient/retryable vs fatal). Arm 1: the `init_core` top-level catch returns rc 1, the same code as any fatal init error, so scripted or agent callers cannot tell a transient stall from a permanent failure. Arm 2: `_create_tracker` exits 1, with the same problem. Arm 3: on the best-effort auto-init path (_cli/_init.py:176-180), a timeout is caught by the existing `except Exception`, but the plan never says what the user sees or whether a later command retries.
scenarios: An agent wrapper treats rc 1 as fatal and never re-runs init, although the condition is transient.
Best-effort auto-init hits a stall, the timeout is swallowed, and the user gets no signal that the store was not created.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the next `rebar init` detects and resolves a tracker left mid-rebase by a timed-out `rebase --continue`, and add a test where a second init after that timeout ends with a clean tracker.
evidence: "Init's rebase recovery re-raises `GitTimedOut` ahead of its `except Exception`, so a timed-out `rebase --continue` is not followed by `rebase --abort`."
Testing only asserts "returns 1 with no `rebase --abort` call"; it says nothing about the next init.
findings.finding: Step 3 makes the rebase recovery re-raise `GitTimedOut` without running `rebase --abort`. That leaves the tracker worktree in an in-progress rebase. The plan does not say what the next `rebar init` does with that state. The pending file only covers `_mount_or_create_branch`/bootstrap, and on the mounted path init would go straight to the ensure sweep. The ensure sweep would then commit on top of a mid-rebase HEAD or fail with a non-timeout error. The promise to "Re-run 'rebar init' to finish" and AC3 are not shown to hold for this arm.
scenarios: `rebase --continue` times out. The user follows the message and re-runs init, which finds a mounted tracker mid-rebase, with no pending-file trigger and no recovery step.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State exactly which arms write `ticket-init.pending`: only when no tracker is mounted (orphan and attach arms), never on the already-mounted re-init path.
evidence: "init writes a `ticket-init.pending` file ... before `_mount_or_create_branch`, and removes it only after the bootstrap completes"
"On the already-mounted path, when the pending file exists, init runs `_finish_bootstrap`"
findings.finding: The conditions for writing the pending file are ambiguous. Step 6 says it is written "before `_mount_or_create_branch`" and that on the mounted path init runs `_finish_bootstrap` "when the pending file exists". If `_mount_or_create_branch` is also reached on re-init of an already-mounted store, every re-init would write the file and then re-run `_finish_bootstrap`. That contradicts "Without the file, re-init behaves as today". The plan also does not say whether the attach-to-existing-remote-branch arm writes the file.
scenarios: Re-init on a healthy mounted store writes the marker. If removal is then skipped by a later timeout, the store is flagged for bootstrap forever.
